issues.legal_issue: A declaratory suit seeking to invalidate a will and sale deed is subject to the fee provision specifically covering cancellation of valuable instruments, even when no consequential relief is sought.
material_facts: The suit sought declarations that a will and a sale deed were void and their cancellation, but sought no consequential relief.
The suit was brought after the testator’s death and concerned property covered by the will.
The plaintiffs valued the property at Rs. 30,00,000 for jurisdiction but paid a fixed court fee under the declaratory-suit provision.
The applicable state amendment specifically provided for court fees in suits involving cancellation or invalidation of instruments relating to property with monetary value.
issues.conclusion: The specific cancellation provision applied, and the court fee had to be computed according to the value of the subject matter; the fixed-fee declaratory provision did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 7(iv-A) of the Court Fees Act, 1870, as amended in Uttar Pradesh, a suit for or involving cancellation or adjudging void or voidable an instrument securing money or other property having value is subject to court fees computed by reference to the subject matter’s value. Article 17(iii) of Schedule II applies to a declaratory suit without consequential relief only where no other provision of the Act provides for the relief claimed. The Court distinguished Suhrid Singh v. Randhir Singh, (2010) 12 SCC 12, because it considered provisions applicable in Punjab and did not examine the Uttar Pradesh amendment.

predicates.declaratory_cancellation_suit: The plaintiff sought a declaration invalidating an instrument and its cancellation.
predicates.instrument_concerns_valuable_property: The instrument at issue secured or related to property having monetary value.
predicates.local_cancellation_fee_rule_applies: The fee rules applicable to the suit specifically provided for cancellation or invalidation suits involving valuable instruments.

issues.definition: When a declaratory cancellation suit involves an instrument concerning valuable property and a specific local cancellation-fee rule applies, the court fee is computed by reference to the subject matter’s value.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decision interpreting different court-fee provisions does not govern a fee dispute when it did not consider the specific amendment applicable to the present suit.
material_facts: The suit arose under a state amendment that specifically addressed court fees for suits involving cancellation or invalidation of valuable instruments.
The cited earlier decision considered provisions applicable in Punjab and did not examine the amendment applicable to this suit.
issues.conclusion: Suhrid Singh v. Randhir Singh did not apply to the present fee dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Suhrid Singh v. Randhir Singh, (2010) 12 SCC 12, addressed Section 7(iv)(c), Section 7(v), and Article 17(iii) as amended in Punjab. Because the effect and scope of the Uttar Pradesh amendment were not considered there, that decision did not determine the present question.

predicates.court_fee_valuation_dispute: The proceeding concerns how a plaintiff must value a suit or pay court fees.
predicates.current_case_uses_distinct_local_fee_rul: The current suit is governed by local court-fee rules different from those addressed in the earlier decision.
predicates.prior_decision_did_not_consider_those_ru: The earlier decision did not consider the local rules that govern the current suit.

issues.definition: In a court-fee valuation dispute, an earlier decision is not controlling when the current suit is governed by distinct local rules that the earlier decision did not consider.
